pool.text: World War I needs led to the construction of the northern part of the Kirov Railway.
Russian Transport Minister Alexander Trepov petitioned to grant urban status to the railway settlement.
After the February Revolution, the town was given its present name on April 3.
Local self-government was organized in Murmansk for the first time during a plenary session.
Resolutions transformed Murmansk Governorate into Murmansk Okrug and made Murmansk the administrative center.
The oldest puppet theater in the city, the Murmansk Puppetry, opened.
The city of Murmansk became a separate administrative division of the okrug.
The Murmansk Regional Drama Theater opened as the largest theater in the city.
The Drama Theater of the Northern Fleet was opened in the city.
A 35.5-meter tall statue named Alyosha depicting a Soviet World War II soldier was installed.
The Hotel Arctic opened, becoming the tallest building above the Arctic Circle.
The city's resistance was commemorated in the formal designation of Murmansk as a Hero City.
The evening newspaper Vecherniy Murmansk has been published since this year.
In the Charter of the Hero City of Murmansk, districts started to be referred to as okrugs.
The territory of Murmansk was expanded when the settlement of Roslyakovo was merged.
